what: A workspace dependency `rustix = { version = "1.1", default-features = false, features = ["fs", "std"] }` in the root Cargo.toml (already in Cargo.lock at 1.1.4 through wasmtime, so no new crate is built). Why: crates/blaze-macro-wasm/src/wasi.rs `Files::resolve` checks that a package path a proc-macro module opens has no link with one `lstat` per part (`Files::links`), so `path_open` of a file d parts deep is d + 4 syscalls; a safe `rustix::fs::openat2(root_fd, rel, .., ResolveFlags::NO_SYMLINKS)` (Linux 5.6+) answers the same question in the open and the descriptor gives the `fstat` and the read, 5 syscalls at any depth, with the existing realpath check kept only for the paths that do have a link (ELOOP), so the semantics stay exact. 20% fewer syscalls on a typical 2-part read (`src/grammar.pest`, `.sqlx/query-*.json`, templates). Section `The WASI host (speed-sol2-usercode-wasm)` of docs/v2/plan/lanes/usercode/speed-of-light-wasm.md. Once it is there, speed-sol2-usercode-wasm (or the usercode lane) writes the change in wasi.rs.

history.note: root Cargo.toml: rustix = { version = "1.1", default-features = false, features = ["fs", "std"] } after rustc-literal-escaper.
